articleTitle: Engineers As Entrepreneurs in Foreign Countries
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Engineers invent new products, determine new methodologies and create new solutions. How can these skills and knowledge be used in setting up a business? Some engineers analyse and fix daily problems with great ideas, and we usually discuss our ideas, with our classmates, friends and family and many believe that it is just only a short step to take the inventions or methodologies to start up as an entrepreneur, but, why are there only several successful engineers-turned- entrepreneurs in foreign countries? This paper discusses who an engineering entrepreneur is and how success is being measured. The author will share his experiences on how he had transited from being an engineer to becoming an entrepreneur in a foreign country. Finally, the paper will discuss the contradicting attributes and route to becoming an entrepreneur and subsequently, a leader to maintain the business.

articleTitle: uBid100: A New Model of Hotel Booking in the Age of AI
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: This article tells the story of a start-up called uBid100, which initiates a new hotel booking model "one person one rate" and breaks the traditional model with the biding policies and AI technology, allowing customers get access to the best deals that is even cheaper than deals on Ctrip platform in just a few seconds. Meanwhile, uBid100 also helps the landlords to switch the cost consuming vacant rooms to earning assets.

articleTitle: Structure and Mechanism of Enterprise Safety Culture Identification
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Based on a ground review of the literature on safety culture, the paper analyzed the forming process of main stream enterprise safety culture and developed a general framework distinguishing three dimensions which enterprise safety culture identification could be studied. The framework described safety culture identification process from three aspects as individual level, group level and organizational level. The results showed that the identification of enterprise safety culture was the key link which makes mainstream enterprise safety culture translated into strong enterprise safety culture.

articleTitle: Entrepreneurship along the New Silk Road : BUSINESS CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES IN THE ONE BELT ONE ROAD INITIATIVE
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: This paper explores the opportunities that arise from the developments of the Belt and Road Initiative, otherwise called `One Belt One Road' (OBOR) Initiative. The OBOR is sometimes called the new Silk Road, following from the historical Silk Road that formed the prosperity of nations `on the Road' from China to the rest of the known world.This paper will give a background to the OBOR, highlight current developments, scope out opportunities for economic integration, policy issues, management challenges and technological enhancement, impact on education, as well as identify possible pitfalls; and highlight activities and opportunities that exist for entrepreneurs to benefit from this global initiative.

articleTitle: Study on Balanced Structure of Organization Based on Structural Balance Theory
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Based on structural balance theory and signed network model, we investigate and analyze the signed social network of A company, and find the optimal balanced structure, and delineate the final signed digraph. In terms of the optimal balanced structure, managers can make employee of company achieve most concordant level and arrange employee with positive social relationships at one department as many as possible. Managers may also use the optimal balanced structure to coordinate the internal conflict, and to design the structure of employee of new program.

articleTitle: Status Quo, Problems and Solutions of College Students’ Innovation and Entrepreneurship under the Policy of “Double First-rate”
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: It has been a trend that college students sign up for technology innovation competitions or start their own businesses after graduation, since the "Double First-rate" policy, i.e. building up "double first-rated" universities, has been implemented and the government has always encouraged education on students’ innovation and entrepreneurship. A study has been conducted to investigate the status quo of students’ innovation and entrepreneurship of Tianjin University through various ways such as case study and field work, questionnaires and interviews, reaching a conclusion that college students lack sufficient knowledge towards innovation and entrepreneurship and that universities should further cultivate students’ practical and comprehensive skills. The essay addresses the problems with the aspects of platform construction, policy support and brand activities with the analysis of specific cases.

articleTitle: An Innovative Syndicate Medium Ecosystem
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: At present, businesses and operators that provide Free Wi-Fi in the world almost emphasize the internet access function of Wi-Fi, while ignoring how to operate the media communication function via Wi-Fi. Users are lost or trapped in the WORLD WIDE WEB internet and classic free Wi-Fi with single channels and multiple clicks. This study explores how emoji Wi-Fi medium technology is creating a new medium in the bitesize internet and driving a technological innovation to turn normal Wi-Fi hotspots into radio stations or brand amplifiers by employing the power of hashtags and emojis. The article focuses on how minimally used Service Set Identifiers (SSIDs) are turned into great marketing assets via an innovative syndicate medium ecosystem, a Hashtags-Over-The-Air platform.

articleTitle: Research on the Crane Scheduling for the Process of Steelmaking-continuous Casting based on Multilevel Heuristic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Production scheduling of steelmaking-continuous casting includes the collaborative optimization of main equipment (multiple converters, refining positions and casters) and auxiliary equipment (multiple cranes). How to make a good scheduling of auxiliary equipment is the key for the real steelmaking production. In this paper, we do research on the scheduling problem of cranes in the process of steelmaking-continuous casting based on mixed integer programming modeling methods, and produce a scheduling scheme which is based on multiple heuristic algorithms. The approach could ensure the quality of scheduling of auxiliary equipment. The optimization methods produced is testified in the production process of steelmaking-continuous casting through a certain large domestic iron and steel enterprise. The results show that the method produced in this paper can smooth the schedule of cranes, promoting the production efficiency and improving the economic benefits of enterprise.

articleTitle: Agile Project Management in New Product Development and Innovation Processes: Challenges and Benefits Beyond Software Domain
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Since the inception of Agile Manifesto and in the 15 years since agile project management (APM) has been in use, it has become a cutting-edge approach practiced, primarily although not exclusively, in the software industry. APM is slowly breaking through into other domains as well. Therefore, the objective of this study is to summarize and critically examine contributions of past research and existing knowledge concerning APM applicability beyond software industry and its co-existence with traditional project management (TPM) practice, and to identify the potential challenges and benefits of APM in innovation and new product development processes. Systematic literature review (SLR) protocol was developed to systematically locate, assess and aggregate the outcomes from all relevant studies in a transparent way. Gaps identified in this SLR will be used to suggest areas for further investigation and to provide a framework for appropriate position of future research activities.

articleTitle: A Blockchain Application for Medical Information Sharing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Medical information are private and medical data are valuable for medical research. Medical information sharing is challenging as the data might be manipulated improperly and revealed during the whole operational process. Medical institutions need shared information for scientific research and develop, on the contrary, privacy issue inhibits the sharing process. In this paper, a new business process and a novel architecture for medical information sharing based on blockchain are proposed. Exploiting the advantage of blockchain in recording transactions, information can be shared and verified among parties like a distributed ledger. On the other hand, medical information can be shared securely between users without an intermediary. The main benefit is that both the information and the traces of the transaction can be distributed stored which avoid manipulation and fraud. Consequently, the value of information can be fully utilized.

articleTitle: Determinants of the Use of Fintech Finance among Chinese Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: FinTech, the merging of finance and modern Internet-based technology, has rapidly presented itself as a disruptor to traditional business financing, notably in the form of crowdfunding and Peer-to-Peer (P2P) lending. In this paper, we examine the determinants of the use of FinTech finance by businesses, with a particular focus on the ownership, governance, and business practices that may modify the relationships with conventional motivations for external finance. Using a comprehensive sample of Chinese hi-tech small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), we find that state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and family firms and financially constrained firms are respectively much less and much more likely to seek FinTech finance. In the Chinese context, we argue that part of this may be because of the relative ease with which SOE SMEs can access cheaper conventional finance through SOE banks. The quality of traditional relationship banking also affects the relative desirability of FinTech financing. As for family firms, we find that innovation, as exemplified by R&D activity, effectively overrides any conventional reluctance to access external finance, suggesting the relative benefits of FinTech finance for innovative high-growth firms.

articleTitle: State-of-the-art and trends of autonomous driving technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Autonomous driving is the research frontier of vehicle engineering and lay a significant impact on automobile industry. Through analysis on Co-word network and technology evolution path in the last 20 years, it finds that the present study on autonomous driving mainly focused on technology of environmental perception, decision making and motion control. Meanwhile, social impacts and regulations can influence this technology through market responses. Achievements and current difficulties in each segment have been discussed in detail. Then, it proposes that two types of ways of future development is available: integration with the high-lever systems, like intelligent transportation system and new energy vehicle; advance in backward subsystems, like sensor system, information processing system and actuating system. Finally, cooperation, data platform and standards and norms are advised to meet the goal of autonomous driving.

articleTitle: Hybrid Fuzzy MCDM Method for Selection of Organizational Innovations in Manufacturing Companies
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Continuous technological improvements have led to paradigm shift in industrial production. New concept, named Industry 4.0, is becoming more and more present in manufacturing companies. Even though advanced technologies are in the focus of Industry 4.0, there is a necessity for organizational improvements as well. Since organizational innovations represent a prerequisite for introduction of advanced technologies in manufacturing companies, there is a need to investigate which are the most appropriate in this context. Particularly, the focus of this paper is on manufacturing companies from developing country. For this purpose, data taken from European Manufacturing Survey are used. In this paper, Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) was employed to determine the weights of criteria, while Preference Ranking Organization Method for Enrichment Evaluations (PROMETHEE) was employed to rank organizational innovations. It was found that in the context of Industry 4.0, organizational innovations related to work organization and design and training and continuing professional development of employees and management of complex systems are the most appropriate for manufacturing companies from developing country.

articleTitle: Identifying Potential Standard Essential Patents Based on Text Mining and Generative Topographic Mapping
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: The identification of the potential standards essential patents (SEPs) can make great contributions to not only the technology management theory, but also to the real practices of establishment and development of enterprise competitiveness and standardization strategy. However, despite the importance of identifying potential SEPs, the approaches to identify potential SEPs lack of adequate mining of existing technical standard text and validation of identification results based on standard updates. Therefore, in this paper, we contribute to resolving this issue by proposing a research model that integrates text mining and the generative topographic mapping (GTM) to effectively identify and verity the potential SEPs based on existing and updated standards. The universal terrestrial radio access (UTRA) technology is selected as a case study. In this case, the TF-IDF algorithm and the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) method are applied to analyze the keywords and technical theme of standard and patent documents, and GTM is used to construct standard and patent map, then the two maps are mapped by the improved similarity algorithm we proposed. Finally, 39 potential SEPs of the technology are identified, 24 of which have been verified, and the other 15 are likely to be included in subsequent standard version. This paper will contribute to the identification of SEPs methodology, and will be of interest to UTRA technology research and development experts.

articleTitle: Return and Volatility Spillovers in the Asia-Pacific Information Technology Stock Markets
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: This paper estimates the directional return and volatility spillovers among information technology stock indices of five countries in the Asia-Pacific area from 1998 to 2017. We use the directional spillover index developed by Diebold and Yilmaz and reveal the pattern of daily return and volatility spillovers in the information technology stock markets, with special focus on the major crisis events in the global financial market as well as in China. We discover that the United States is the main contributor to both return and volatility spillovers during the entire period, while other countries mainly receive spillovers from the United Sates. We also find drastic spillovers in periods not noticed by previous studies. The results suggest that the global information technology stock markets are closely connected and have some distinct features that need deeper investigations, especially in a world more and more reliant on technology development.

articleTitle: Role of Startup’s Intellectual Property in VCs Investment Decision-Making: Evidence from Russia
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: While most academic papers claim that intellectual property (IP) rights, and especially patents, are useful and necessary for early-stage startups, evidence from the practice frequently demonstrates the opposite: patents are excessive and not of the great value for early-stage ventures. In this study, we aim to provide deeper understanding of the described contradiction and to try to explain why it exists. To achieve the goal, we interviewed 17 venture capitalists (VCs) based in Russia, who actively invest in startups on international scene and in Russia. The results from our sample suggest that IP may be more important for startups in the later stages, and not equally useful at the beginning of their development. We believe that main differentiator between early and later stages of a startup (which crucially influences on the role and value of its IP in the eyes of VCs) is not size or age, but the validation of startup's business model. This proposition is going be tested in the further research.

articleTitle: Sustainability for the Holistic Ecosystem: Regulation Guide Designing for the Prevalent Technology Development of China Emerging Communications: Big Data, IoT, 5G etc.
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: The remembrance of the deeds of past paths is the best guide for the future. This paper is a result of learned lessons from the past four decades (1978 to 2018) in the China communication fields in regard to its huge success and progress. Actor-Network Theory (ANT) will be used and Enterprise Architecture Management (EAM) to evaluate the nine areas which have acted as the main successful factors. Through telecommunications and internet connections, the world has become as interconnected as a family. Holistic ecosystem regulation will prevent violation of the healthy developments of new technologies. This article seeks to present guidelines for the regulations which will benefit the sustainability for future and several worlds’ experiences are included in this study. Given that we pay for what we buy, the price paid for the new technology development needs to be balanced with what it will be achieved. Balance is the key for world’s holistic ecosystem. When you already stand on the top of the world, what will be next? The best way is that you take care of your neighbors’ needs. This is China’s Silk Road building from land and sea to support others.

articleTitle: The Effect of Collaboration with Different Partners: A Contingency Model
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Focusing on innovation collaboration, this paper examines the different roles of three types of innovation collaboration on firms' innovation performance, and assesses whether the effect of such collaboration is conditional on internal and external context characteristics in emerging economies. The regression results reveal that both the collaboration with science-based partners and the collaboration with foreign business partners are positively related to a firm's innovation performance, while collaboration with domestic business partners is negatively related to a firm's innovation performance. Our research also shows that prior knowledge stock positively moderates the influence of collaboration with both foreign business partners and science-based partners, while negatively moderates the influence of collaboration with domestic business partners; connections to institutional structure positively moderates the influence of collaboration with foreign business partners, while negatively moderates the influence of collaboration with science-based partners collaboration with domestic business partners. Our research contributes to existing open innovation research.

articleTitle: Reciprocal complementarity in use between the knowledge linkages and organizational innovation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: External knowledge has becoming critical factor for firms' innovation development. This study examines the relationship among knowledge linkages diversity, organizational innovation, and firm innovation performance. We anchor on the complementarity-in-use and knowledge-based perspective to provide a theoretical base in examining the how knowledge linkages diversity drive the innovation performance, and how organizational innovation influence the complementary between external knowledge linkages and innovation performance. We argue that prior research gas ignored that both capabilities are interrelated and complementary in sharing firms' innovativeness. Drawing on the third Community Innovation Survey (CIS III), we conduct an empirical study to tests the hypotheses and the relationship among knowledge linkages diversity, organizational innovation and innovation performance. We found external knowledge linkages has an inverted U-shaped and significant effect on the firm innovation performance. In particular we find that availability of organizational innovation mitigates the effect of knowledge linkages diversity on innovation performance when diverse knowledge linkage is moderate and complements it as innovation resources become excessive. Furthermore, the empirical result also found that the organizational innovation has a positive and significant effect on firm innovation performance. Our findings have important implications for managers of firms innovation strategic decisions and the degree to which they acquire external knowledge in innovation deploying.

articleTitle: Research on Regional Independent Innovation and Open Innovation Optimization Strategy under Innovation Driving Strategy : Taking the biomedical industry of China as an example
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: With China's economic development entering the new normal, it is difficult to maintain further growth by relying on the traditional extensive mode of development. So "Innovation driven" has become one of the major strategies to drive the country's overall development. Under the background of innovation driven development strategy, independent innovation and open innovation have been emphasized. Xi Jinping, Chinese President, suggested that we should promote independent innovation in the background of open innovation. Because specific innovation relations often need to adopt adapted innovation strategy, how to optimize independent innovation strategy under open background and how to improve open innovation strategy under the guideline of independent innovation is the key issue for further research and national development. Therefore, taking the biological industry as an example, we use social network analysis method to build intra-regional and inter-regional innovation networks in 31 provinces during 1985-2013. And based on input-output theory, technology spillover effect and social capital theory, we empirically analyses the role of independent innovation investment in regional independent innovation and the moderating effect of open innovation on the relationship between independent innovation input and regional innovation output. The study finds that: regional R&D investment, including capital investment and personnel investment, will promote its innovative output, but regional international introduction, including import and FDI, will inhibit its innovation output. In addition, for intra-regional collaboration innovation, its network average clustering coefficient and density will promote the positive relationship between R&D investment and innovation output, but it will worsen the role of international introduction in restraining innovation output. For the inter-regional collaboration innovation, the regional clustering coefficient is beneficial to the promotion of R&D investment to the innovation output, but its network dependence plays an opposite role; moreover, the network dependence and betweenness centrality of the region will exacerbate the inhibitory effect of international introduction on innovative output. Finally, according to the above conclusions, we not only propose an optimization strategy for the independent innovation under the open innovation background, but also provide some suggestions for the open innovation under the policy of independent innovation.

articleTitle: Mapping Entrepreneurial Ecosystem of China:a Multi-Perspective Comparison
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Entrepreneurial Ecosystem is not only the catalyst for steady economic development. It is an important factor to reverse the economic slowdown. "Popular innovation and entrepreneurship" can hardly boost China developing fast without the support of well Entrepreneurial Ecosystem. This paper makes a vertical comparison for the past five year about entrepreneurial ecosystem in China and a horizontal comparison between China and other countries which are in the same development stage or higher stage according to Global Competitive Reports to address Chinese Entrepreneurial Ecosystem further. Results show that most of the factors are showing an improving trend, especially financing for Entrepreneurs, Governmental Support and Policies for Entrepreneurship, Internal Market Dynamics, Cultural and Social Norms etc. But, R&D Transfer and Commercial, Professional Infrastructure should be improved urgently. This paper will benefit "mass entrepreneurship and innovation" further and provide experience to other followers from developing countries.

articleTitle: Regional comparative research on innovation and entrepreneurship policy from the perspective of policy tool
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: With the continuous and embedded implementation of "Public Entrepreneurship and Mass Innovation" strategies in China, a series of policies have been promulgated by the central and regional government in order to promote the innovation and entrepreneurship. It is the fact that both the central and local governments are China's industrial policy makers, which certainly cause differences in the relevant industrial policy content. Normally, the central government makes decisions from an overall point of view, while local governments tend to be practical on policymaking. Based on gathering a series of policy documents promulgated by the central government and three first-tier cities including Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen, which regarding to innovation and entrepreneurship during the past ten years, this paper constructs a classification of policy tool of these policies. Then, the paper conducts a comparison analysis of these three cities' innovation and entrepreneurship policies from the perspective of policy tool. Based on the aforesaid analysis, the paper proposes suggestions to promote China's innovation and entrepreneurship.

articleTitle: Why is Siemens establishing its robotics R&D centers in China? A case study on the Siemens industrial robot project
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: China has been transforming its development strategy from an investment-driven to an innovation-led one. Recent government policies (e.g., "Made in China 2025") have shown the country's ambition to upgrade its manufacturing industry. Meanwhile, the technological environments and market conditions in China have also been changing rapidly. All these changes in terms of government policies, technological environments, and market conditions bring both opportunities and challenges for multinational enterprises (MNEs) in China. How should MNEs react to such new realities? As one leading MNE with a long history in the Chinese market, Siemens has been adapting its global R&D strategies, establishing its R&D centers of industrial robots in China. This represents an interesting case to academic researchers, industry practitioners, as well as policy makers. To better understand the co-evolution of MNEs and China's innovation systems, we conducted this case study project on the Siemens innovation about industrial robots. The research shows that, on the one hand, Siemens' decision of conducting R&D on industrial robots in China is driven by China's evolving host-country environments. On the other hand, the changing R&D strategies of Siemens in China also have impacts on China's innovation system, helping domestic manufacturers to make more advanced robots.

articleTitle: Antecedents of Local Market Initiative: An Investigation of Chinese Subsidiaries
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: This study aims to advance research on local market initiative, a form of subsidiary initiative that emanates from new opportunities in the local marketplace. Given that market-seeking MNCs in China face particular pressures stemming from local market conditions, China is particularly relevant research site to examine the concept. Drawing on agency theory, resource dependence theory and the resource based view of the firm and using survey data from 75 subsidiaries of German manufacturing companies in China, the effects of subsidiary autonomy and entrepreneurial culture on local market initiative are analyzed. The results provide evidence that both subsidiary autonomy and the presence of an entrepreneurial culture are associated with local market initiative. This research has major implications for MNCs and their market-seeking subsidiaries abroad and its designated focus on local market initiative constitutes a milestone in subsidiary initiative research.

articleTitle: The effect of Triple helix and innovative local community on the sustainable entrepreneurship in resource dependent region of China
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: During recent years, resource dependent regions in China are facing great transitional challenges in transforming into new sustainable development. Entrepreneurship is considered to be vital vehicle in this process. Based on prior research, this research tries to provide deeper view about the effects of Triple Helix and innovative local community on sustainable entrepreneurship. A survey of 1224 university students joined in Entrepreneur Association was carried out to support this theorized model. The main findings of this research suggest that university undergraduates in resource dependent regions are improved to be risk seeking and fill with courage quotient in break away with market barriers. This process involves different collaboration, and should be carried out by the type of universities. For the non-science and engineering university, the marginal effect of different stakeholders on sustainable entrepreneurship are strengthened when adding in the trilateral interact effect among university, innovative local community and the government. When considering the science and engineering universities, triple cooperation mode is the most efficient way compared with other cooperation (bilateral and quadrilateral) modes in fostering sustainable entrepreneurship. These findings contribute to literature streams on both of sustainable entrepreneurship and sustainable transition. Finally, four kinds of special strategies for different stakeholders were recommended by extending our results.

articleTitle: The Double Channel Synergy of Motivation in Predicting Entrepreneur’s Creativity and Firm Innovation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: In this research, the role of motivational impact on entrepreneur's creativity and the following startup innovation was discussed and examined. Drawing on the componential model of creativity (Amabile, 1983, 1988, 1996) and the motivated information processing in group model (MIP-G model; De Dreu et al., 2008a, 2008b), I proposed that creativity is influenced by intrinsic motivation, prosocial motivation and furthermore, motivational synergy through these two channels. In the internal channel, intrinsic motivation is critical for creativity by promoting "the individual's positive reaction to qualities of the task itself" (Amabile, 1996, p. 115). In the external channel, however, taking social information processes (Salancik, & Pfeffer, 1978) as a driving force, the minority dissent will influence the team by producing individual creativity (De Dreu et al., 2008a; 2008b) and improving group performance (Gong et al., 2013) when the members have high prosocial motivation. Under the interaction of internal channel and external channel, the intrinsic motivation will enhance the impact of prosocial motivation on individual creativity. Hypotheses were proposed based on the theoretical framework and tested according to the evidence from organizational field research. Implications for motivation as driving force of creativity are discussed.

articleTitle: Does the Sharing Economy Benefits the Relationship Between External Network Utilization and Innovation Performance?
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Sharing economy grow dramatically and influence innovation activities and operation of firms especially small-and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in high-tech industries. Based on social capital theory, we argue that external net utilization could enhance innovation performance in SMEs when the internal network does not effect. Crowd-innovation space and sharing platform which viewed as part of sharing economy benefits the relationship between external network utilization and innovation performance. Even though external network utilization is weak in SMEs, crowd-innovation space and sharing platform could improve their innovation performance. Sharing databases could not moderate the relationship between external network utilization and innovation performance, but these can benefit innovation performance.

articleTitle: Effects of relative power imbalance in the ecosystem on innovation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Successful innovation cannot be separated from knowledge resources outside. Innovation ecosystem describe interactions and inter-linkages between organizations and provide related complementary technology and asset for value creation and appropriation through innovation. In this paper, we explore power structure in the ecosystem impact on innovation performance of the focal firm. Relative power imbalance is one of the power structure in the ecosystem, which predicts the willing of actors to share their knowledge with other actors and the focal firm. Results based on a panel data of 396 observations about focal firms and their suppliers show that relative power imbalance has a negative effect on innovation performance, but firm age and high-tech certification positively moderate this relationship. These results contribute to the understanding about roles of power structure and knowledge sharing in ecosystem management.

articleTitle: CEO Exit after IPO: Which Wealth Matters?
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: IPOs are typically viewed as the peak of entrepreneurial success. However, CEOs in those entrepreneurial firms often leave after the IPOs to harvest their investment. The understanding of such voluntary exit remains rudimentary in small business and entrepreneurial settings. We examine the impact of both CEOs' financial and socioemotional wealth on their exit decisions after IPOs. The findings show that CEOs with greater financial wealth are more likely to stay with the firm initially, but they become more likely to leave after certain threshold. We also find that socioemotional wealth negatively moderates the predications of financial wealth on exit.

articleTitle: Open Innovation of SMEs - An Innovation Ecosystem Perspective
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: In this paper we study SMEs' open innovation from an innovation ecosystem perspective. We divide an SME's external linkages with its partners in an innovation ecosystem into two types (i.e. the Linkages of an SME with its Prominent Organisations (LPO) and the Linkages of the SEM with its Service Intermediaries (LSI)). We then examine the relationships between LPO (and LSI) and the SME's innovation performance, and analyse the moderating effects of the SME's absorptive capacity on the two relationships. Research results support a positive relationship between LPO and SMEs' innovation performance, and a positive relationship between LSI and SMEs' innovation performance and a positive relationship between LSI and LPO. In addition, research results shows that when measured by R&D Intensity SMEs' absorptive capacity negatively moderates the relationships between LPO (and LSI) and SMEs' innovation performance, whereas when measured by IT adoption, SMEs' absorptive capacity positively moderates the two relationships. Relevant theoretical and managerial contributions are discussed.

articleTitle: Conceptualising Entreprenurial Ecosystems: Definition, Configurations and Health
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: This paper conceptualises entrepreneurial ecosystems (EE) by addressing their definition, configurations and health. We define EE dynamically and highlight the interactions between value creation and location. We explore patterns of EE by two dimensions: driving forces varying by locations and value creation types. We also propose three dimensions that characterise EE health: basic functions, resilience and adaptation. Our theorizing contributes to entrepreneurship literatures by linking how entrepreneurs access resources to EE, and business ecosystem literatures by connecting location with value creation.

abstract: The following topics are dealt with: innovation management; organisational aspects; investment; small-to-medium enterprises; knowledge management; Internet; commerce; personnel; strategic planning; government policies.
